a hybrid semiconductor-superconductors nanowire on top of a magnetic stripe phase experiences a large synthetic spinorbit coupling, which can support the formation and control of MBS.

the magnetic texture from the fringing field of a magnetic stripe phase can induce topological superconductivity in a semiconductor nanowire on top of it, and that the current flowing through a magnetic stripe can be used to tune the topological phase and the MBS.
a current through a magnetic film can induce a topological phase in a proximitized semiconductor nanowire.

the physics of the topological phase transition in hybrid semiconductor-superconducting nanostructures, and the development of a platform for the control and manipulation of Majorana bound state.
the study of the interplay between magnetic and superconducting orders and their interplay with spin-orbit interactions and Zeeman coupling.
the development of new materials and new methods of their processing, which are based on the use of nanotechnology.

we have demonstrated that the current-controlled MBS formation in the hybrid semiconductor-super-conductor-nanowire on the magnetic stripe phase is a viable and promising platform for the realization of Majorana bound state based quantum devices.
the current flowing through a magnetic stripe phase can be used to control the MBS.
we have shown a platform that allows for non-invasive current controlled Majorana bound states in a hybrid semiconductor-superconductor nanowire.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new platform to create and control Majorana bound states by passing a charge-current through the magnetic film underneath the nanowire.
we have proposed a new platform to host MBS, which is based on a semiconductor nanowire on a ferromagnetic stripe phase.
the current-controlled Majorana bound states can be realized by using magnetic stripes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MBS are robust against the inhomogeneity of the magnetic textures and can be tuned by current flowing through the underlying magnetic stripes.
the current-controlled Majorana bound states in the proposed platform can be used as a new type of spintronic devices.
current-controlled topological phase transitions can be realized in a hybrid semiconductor-superconductors system with the magnetic texture of the underlying magnetic film.
